claims.text: IL-6 inhibitors (tocilizumab, sarilumab) work in patients with an incomplete response to other biologics, alone or with methotrexate or another conventional DMARD.
claims.quote: Interleukin (IL)-6 inhibitors (eg, tocilizumab, sarilumab) have clinical efficacy in patients who have responded incompletely to other biologic agents. It may be used as monotherapy but can also be given in combination with methotrexate or another conventional synthetic DMARD.
claims.locator: Pharmacologic Therapy for Rheumatoid Arthritis › Biologic DMARDs

claims.text: Abatacept (CTLA-4 fusion protein) is indicated after an inadequate response to other DMARDs.
claims.quote: Abatacept, a soluble fusion cytotoxic T lymphocyte-associated antigen 4 (CTLA-4) immunoglobulin, is indicated for patients with rheumatoid arthritis with an inadequate response to other DMARDs.
claims.locator: Pharmacologic Therapy for Rheumatoid Arthritis › Biologic DMARDs

claims.text: Rituximab (anti-CD20, depletes B cells) is for refractory RA; response is often delayed but may last 6 months. Mild infusion reactions are common; rare PML and hepatitis B reactivation.
claims.quote: Rituximab is an anti-CD 20 antibody that depletes B cells. It can be used in patients refractory to other treatments. Response is often delayed but may last 6 months. The course can be repeated after 6 months. Mild infusion reactions are common, and analgesia, corticosteroids, diphenhydramine, or a combination may need to be given concomitantly. Rituximab therapy has rarely been associated with progressive multifocal leukoencephalopathy (as have other immunosuppressive agents), mucocutaneous reactions, delayed leukopenia, and hepatitis B reactivation with hepatic necrosis.
claims.locator: Pharmacologic Therapy for Rheumatoid Arthritis › Biologic DMARDs
